records.note: Describes the current 6-hour cap in the category III codes and adds 'may not be enough'. No deciding body, no code change and no observable criterion. The registry holds no CPT monitoring-hour event. Rejection stands.
'The REMS program will drive the reimbursement infrastructure' names no decision and no threshold. A causal claim about how one thing shapes another is not a checkable event. Rejection stands.

'A robust new code set will need to be the case' is a necessity claim, not an event. No code-setting body, no code and no benchmark for 'robust'. The registry holds no psychedelic billing-code event. Rejection stands.
'Will need complexity based billing and longer monitoring' states what the compounds require, not what a payer or regulator does. No threshold for 'longer' and no deciding body. Rejection stands.
'Commercially and clinically disastrous' is a value judgment about a hypothetical. No entity, no event and no observable criterion. Rejection stands.
'An access barrier measured in years' inside a recommendation. 'Years' is a description of the barrier, not a horizon for an event, and 'access barrier' has no benchmark. Rejection stands.

'A G/J Code ... is likely to be necessary' is a recommendation about what the code set should contain. No body issues a named code by a named date, and the registry holds no buy-and-bill code event. Rejection stands.
'Likely to be expensive drugs' names no drug, no price and no series. A comparative without a benchmark. Rejection stands.
'These drugs are likely to rise in price' gives no asset, no threshold and no price series. A quantity_threshold event cannot be written without inventing all three. Rejection stands.
'Coverage decisions will require economic data' names no payer, no treatment and no published policy. It states a precondition, not a coverage decision. Rejection stands.
'Undercut financial support ... limiting future innovation' has no company, no series and no threshold. Market sentiment is not an observable event here. Rejection stands.

'What is acceptable according to Medicare is likely to be followed by other payors' names no treatment, no policy and no payer that must follow. No coverage_decision event can be written. Rejection stands.

'It may be teams of Psychiatrist and other health professionals' names no drug, no label text and no deciding body. The registry prescriber-restriction events are written on midomafetamine labeling, which this claim does not name. Rejection stands.
A list of what a psychedelic-capable clinic will require. No third party decides it, and no countable set of clinics or date is given. Rejection stands.
Conditional on an unobservable antecedent ('if reimbursement does not count for them'). 'Large, vertically integrated organizations' is not a countable set. Rejection stands.
'Set and setting are likely to be crucial factors' has no entity, no event and no test for 'crucial'. Rejection stands.
'Could make [consolidation] more common place' is a comparative with no benchmark, no named series and no company. Rejection stands.
'Access will narrow' gives no metric, no series and no threshold, and the antecedent (independent practices losing money at payer rates) is not observable in a named source. Rejection stands.

Evaluates a hypothetical FDA requirement ('would function as a geographic access restriction without a corresponding safety benefit') rather than forecasting that the FDA imposes it. No observable criterion. Rejection stands.
Present-tense description of the class ('cannot reach patients without clinicians ... in the loop'), with no future state asserted and no confidence phrase. Better code than the earlier VAGUE.

records.stage_note: No psilocybin, LSD or MDMA drug product had FDA approval at the statement date; the claim presupposes approvals to come, and E-0067 is void if none occurs in the window.
records.note: Denies retail pharmacy-benefit distribution for the coming psychedelic therapies. Same asset and outcome type as E-0067 (a psilocybin, LSD or MDMA product approved with retail-pharmacy dispensing), which the registry now holds. 'Will not' sets bin A with asserts false. No time words, so the item is undated. The FDA decides and none of the forecaster's affiliations is named in the event.
'The questions that will determine whether approved psychedelic therapies reach the patients' names no decision and no measurable reach. Rejection stands.

records.stage_note: Accelerated TMS (SNT) carries an FDA authorization for major depressive disorder at the statement date; no accelerated iTBS randomized trial in bipolar depression is named in the post.
records.note: Efficacy call on accelerated TMS, specifically SNT, in bipolar depression. Same asset and outcome type as E-0006, whose criterion covers an accelerated iTBS randomized trial in a depressive disorder. 'Likely' sets bin B. The label-change sentence is a necessity claim and is not coded here. No time words, so the item is undated. Affiliated: the forecaster is an accelerated TMS clinician and trial site (Radial, Acacia), as in owen-1947.

event.asset: Intravenous (IV) ketamine for bipolar depression: US health plan coverage
event.entity: US health insurers, health plans and public programs (commercial plans, Medicare, Medicaid or the VA)
event.title: A US health plan covers IV ketamine for bipolar depression
event.proposition: A US health insurer, health plan or public program publishes a coverage policy that covers intravenous ketamine for bipolar depression.
event.criterion: TRUE on the effective date of a published medical or coverage policy, fee schedule entry, national coverage determination, local coverage determination or public policy bulletin from a US health insurer, health plan or public program (a commercial plan, Medicare, Medicaid or the VA) that lists intravenous ketamine as covered or medically necessary for bipolar depression. A policy that covers esketamine (Spravato), a policy limited to major depressive disorder, an individual case exception, coverage limited to a clinical trial, and a payment for the infusion visit without the drug do not count. FALSE at the deadline when no such policy is in force. Resolved on the payer's published policy bulletin and the CMS Medicare Coverage Database.

resolution_source.name: Payer medical policy bulletins; CMS Medicare Coverage Database

readings: 'Meaningful coverage' is read as at least one published US health plan coverage policy for the indication; the forecaster names no payer, so any US health plan or public program counts, as in E-0116.
'IV ketamine. For bipolar depression.' fixes the asset and the indication; esketamine is a different product and does not count.
The KET-BD trial result is the reason the forecaster gives, not part of the criterion.

records.phrase: unlikely to lead to meaningful coverage
records.stage_note: IV ketamine is a generic drug used off label for bipolar depression at the statement date, with the academic KET-BD result just reported and no sponsor pursuing a label. No class in base-rates.json covers a payer coverage decision.
records.note: A named treatment (IV ketamine), a named indication (bipolar depression) and a named outcome type (payer coverage) support an event, so the claim is recovered from the earlier VAGUE. The registry holds no IV ketamine coverage event, so a new one is proposed on the pattern of E-0116. 'Unlikely' sets bin D with asserts true. No time words, so the item is undated. Payers decide and none of the forecaster's affiliations is named in the event.
A structural claim about which pitch wins funding. No company, no countable set of programs, no series and no date. Rejection stands.
'Less true financially than emotionally' names no company, no return and no series. A comparative without a benchmark. Rejection stands.
'We'll be questioning why we ever did this with SSRIs' names no guideline, no body and no prescribing series. A change of opinion in the field is not observable in a named source. Rejection stands.
Fundraising call to action. 'More people get access' and 'more research' are quantifiers with no countable set, no threshold and no series. Rejection stands.
